sentences.text:
This application coming on for admission this day, the court passed the following:
 ORDER 1.
The applicant has filed this second bail application u/S.439 Cr.P.C for grant of bail.

Applicant has been arrested on 06.10.2023 by Police Station- Kampoo, District Gwalior in connection with Crime No.273/2022, registered for offence punishable under Sections 366, 376, 368, 506, 34 of IPC.

sentences.text: It is the submission of learned counsel for applicant that earlier bail was granted to the applicant vide order dated 12.07.2022 in M.Cr.C. No.33836/2022 after suffering confinement for around one month.
It was a case of consent prima facie and after considering the rival submissions bail was granted.

However, because of allegations of complainant that after grant of bail application applicant posted certain photographs on social media, therefore, application for cancellation of bail was preferred in which applicant surrendered on 6.10.2023 and now suffering confinement since then.
He learnt the lesson hard way and now separate case has been registered against him for offence under Section 67 of I.T. Act, and therefore, said offence is bailable in nature.
Applicant does not bear any criminal record.
However, he undertakes that he will not cause any embarrassment or harassment to the prosecutrix in any manner in person through somebody else or through some digital mode.
Under these grounds, he prayed for bail.
3 . Learned counsel for the respondent/State opposed the prayer and prayed for dismissal of application.

4. Learned counsel for complainant submits that after photographs being posted over social media,
mobile of applicant which was used in such mischief is yet to be recovered from his possession.

Therefore, police be directed to retrieve the same in accordance with law.
5.
Heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the case diary.

6. Considering the rival submissions advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and nature of allegation which is primarily under Section 67 of I.T. Act, without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court intends to allow the application but with certain stringent conditions.

Accordingly,
the application is allowed.

It is hereby directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with two solvent sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of trial Court.

8. Application stands allowed and disposed of.
9. A copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance and information.
10. Certified Copy as per rules.
(ANAND PATHAK) JUDGE Van VANDANA VERMA 2023.10.19 16:38:45 +05'30'
